activities.instructions: Use the source-based options to complete this activity.
activities.sourceTextSummary: Generated from Accountancy - Financial Accounting - 1, Chapter Chapter 2.

correctItems.text: P artnership is an agreement between two or more persons (called partners) for sharing the profits of a business carried on by all or any of them acting for all.
Any change in the existing agreement amounts to reconstitution of the partnership firm.
This results in an end of the existing agreement and a new agreement comes into being with a changed relationship among the members of the partnership firm and/or their composition.
For example, Hari and Haqque are partners sharing profits in the ratio of Reconstitution of a Partnership Firm - Admission of a Partner Reprint 2025-26 49 Admission of a Partner 3:2.

activities.modelAnswer: P artnership is an agreement between two or more persons (called partners) for sharing the profits of a business carried on by all or any of them acting for all. Any change in the existing agreement amounts to reconstitution of the partnership firm. This results in an end of the existing agreement and a new agreement comes into being with a changed relationship among the members of the partnership firm and/or their composition. correctItems.text: Death of a partner: Partnership may also stand reconstituted on death of a partner, if the remaining partners decide to continue the business of the firm as usual.
For example, X,Y and Z are partners in a firm sharing profits in the ratio 3:2:1.
Y and Z decide to carry on the business sharing future profits equally.
The continuity of business by Y and Z sharing future profits equally leads to reconstitution of the firm.
